pr.title: coverage: Discard spans that fill the entire function body
pr.description:
While debugging some other coverage changes, I discovered a frustrating inconsistency that occurs in functions containing closures, if they end with an implicit `()` return instead of an explicit trailing-expression.

This turns out to have been caused by the corresponding node in MIR having a span that covers the entire function body. When preparing coverage spans, any span that fills the whole body tends to cause more harm than good, so this PR detects and discards those spans.

(This isn't the first time whole-body spans have caused problems; we also eliminated some of them in #118525.)
pr.author: Zalathar

analysis.summary: Coverage span extraction must discard MIR statement/terminator spans that fill the entire function body, because those spans usually represent compiler-inserted code (e.g. implicit `()` return) and produce inconsistent/unhelpful coverage mappings, especially inside closures.
analysis.originalLogic: In `bcb_to_initial_coverage_spans`, each MIR statement span and terminator span was passed directly through `unexpand_into_body_span_with_visible_macro(expn_span, body_span)`; whatever `(span, visible_macro)` it returned was turned into a `SpanFromMir` and included in the initial coverage spans. There was no check rejecting a span that covered the whole body.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Retain coverage spans whose unexpanded span is source-equal to the whole function body. In practice the implicit `()` return terminator in a function containing closures has a whole-body span; keeping it creates a coverage region covering the entire body, so a closure's closing brace/body gets mapped to the enclosing function's counter and appears executed (or otherwise inconsistent between explicit trailing `()` and implicit unit return).
analysis.inputDomain: Rust functions/closures instrumented for coverage whose MIR contains statements or terminators with spans covering the entire body, notably implicit unit returns (`()`), macro-expanded code, and closure-like bodies. Construct a pair of functions differing only in explicit trailing-expression `()` return vs implicit `()` return, both containing a closure.
analysis.trigger: A MIR statement or terminator's span, after `unexpand_into_body_span_with_visible_macro`, satisfies `span.source_equal(body_span)`; the terminator for the implicit unit return is the concrete case reported for functions with closures.
preconditions: The function body has a closure and ends with an implicit `()` return rather than an explicit trailing expression.
The relevant MIR node's span fills the function body.
pitfalls: Do not simply drop all spans from coverage processing; only spans source-equal to the whole body should be discarded after unexpansion.
Dropping legitimate nested/last-expression spans would lose coverage.
The inconsistency only manifests as different coverage between explicit and implicit unit returns; comparing counter bytes alone without also checking the rendered coverage regions can miss it.
Whole-body spans may also arise from macro expansion and closures, so test multiple shapes.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a coverage regression test (`tests/coverage/closure_unit_return.rs`) with `explicit_unit` and `implicit_unit` functions whose closures are identical and whose only difference is `()` as a trailing expression vs implicit unit return. Check both `.cov-map` raw mapping bytes and rendered `.coverage` regions; after the fix the implicit function's closure closing brace should not be marked executed. Also update/verify existing coverage tests with whole-body spans (`coverage_attr_closure`, `inline-dead`, `macro_name_span`, `unicode`). The test harness compares expected `.cov-map`/`.coverage` output; no compiler execution was performed here.
